community.reason: Level 2. The report shows specific current community investment: a Volunteer Time Off program with 33% employee participation (E1) and site-based donations and fundraising (E2). It also shows extensive employee development (E3, E4). The community investment gives only a participation rate, with no dollars, volunteer hours or beneficiaries, so reach is not shown to be substantial. When torn, pick the lower level. Employee development alone is capped at 2.

That is substantial against roughly 2,900 employees. Participation in the WBCSD LEAP program for women executives (E6) adds a smaller internal practice. There is no customer-access or connecting-communities activity at business scale that would support level 4.

notes: The Item 7 (targeted) section was empty, meaning no MD&A paragraphs matched the theme terms. The Human Capital section is about 340 words, but most of it covers headcount by country, tenure, collective bargaining and safety metrics (RIR 0.26, DART 0.13). Only about 60 words address training, development or inclusion, and only in general terms, so Community and Cross-cultural are marked insufficient under condition 2. The Board's 'Environmental Sustainability and Community Committee' is only a committee name and does not count as an activity. Employee location percentages (80% US, 14% Canada, 6% UK) are geographic and are not demographics of underrepresented groups. 'Joint venture' references (Blue Point, PLNL, CHS strategic venture) are entrepreneurship traps and were excluded. A 'license to use certain intellectual property' contributed to Blue Point is not creative licensing and was excluded. Both Community and Cross-cultural have insufficient coverage, so this company qualifies for the automated second look using the company's sustainability report from www.cfindustries.com.
